transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, doctor, my wife sent me down here. It's... it's about the men at the domino table. We play down at the center. Mostly just draw dominoes, you know. I used to play with my brother a lot before he passed back in '98. We'd sit out on the porch for hours. 

But lately, the men there, they've been giving these little messages. Just meant for me. And the radio announcer does it too. I got one of those little radios I keep out in the garage... bought it at Sears a long, long time ago. Still works fine, you just have to wiggle the dial a bit to get the static out. 

But anyway, the announcer and the domino men, they slip in these messages. And even when my wife says it is just talk—she's always fussing about something, she was just fussing about me leaving the garden hose out this morning—but I know what I hear. I know they are warning me to be careful. That's why I came in.
How long have you been noticing these messages?

Well, let me think on that. I reckon the voices and those special messages... they've been happening on and off for about nine months now. Started right around the time I had to get the alternator fixed on my old Ford. You know, they just don't make parts for those trucks like they used to. I took it down to Earl's shop. Earl's a good boy, his daddy and I used to go fishing out at Miller's Pond before the county drained it. Caught a bass out there once that was near on five pounds, fought me for twenty minutes. Best eating fish we had all year. But yeah, nine months of it, coming and going. Earl charged me an arm and a leg for that alternator, though. I told my wife we ought to just sell the truck, but she won't hear of it. She says she needs it for hauling her garden supplies.
When you mention hearing voices, do you hear them speaking even when the radio is off and nobody is around?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. Some afternoons, when the house is just dead quiet... you know, my wife goes down to her sister's on Tuesdays to help with the quilting, they've been making this big star pattern quilt for the church auction. Beautiful thing, all blues and yellows. Her sister's got that big sunroom on the back of her house, gets real hot in the summer though. But anyway, when she's gone and it's quiet, I'll be sitting there and I'll hear my old friend call my name right from the porch. Or sometimes he's humming one of those old choir songs we used to sing. Clear as day, like he's standing right there next to the rocking chair. That rocking chair needs fixing, actually. One of the spindles came loose when my grandson was visiting last Easter. Boy was climbing all over it like a monkey. I told him to get down, but you know how kids are nowadays, they just don't listen. They've got their faces stuck in those little screens all the time. Can't even have a decent conversation with 'em.
Have you noticed any difficulties with your memory recently?

Memory? No, I haven't noticed any trouble with that. My memory's sharp as a tack, mostly. I mean, just yesterday I remembered to pick up the exact brand of coffee my wife likes from the grocery store without her even having to write it down. Maxwell House, the blue tin. 

Though, I'll tell you, they went and moved everything around at the store again. Drives me absolutely up the wall when they do that. The manager there, young fella named Tim—wears these thick glasses, looks like he's about twelve years old, honestly—he moved all the canned peaches all the way over to aisle four. Took me a good ten minutes to find them. I used to buy those exact same peaches for my mother back when she was living over on Elm Street. She had this little yellow house with a big old oak tree out front. Dropped acorns all over the driveway, sounded like hail when you drove over 'em in the winter. We used to have to sweep them up every Sunday before church, otherwise folks would twist an ankle walking up to the door. Pastor Miller came over once and nearly went flying. He was a good preacher, though. Spoke real loud, you never fell asleep in his pews.
Do you have any medical conditions or physical health problems that you are currently being treated for?

Medical problems? No, sir, I don't have anything like that I'm seeing a doctor for. I've always had a real strong constitution, you know? Never needed much doctoring at all. My granddaddy always said a raw clove of garlic and a good night's sleep would keep the sickness away. He used to grow his own garlic out behind the old tractor shed. Biggest bulbs you ever did see. He'd string 'em up right there in the kitchen, smelled to high heaven, but my grandma never complained. She was an absolute saint, that woman. Used to bake these wild blackberry pies... we'd go picking down by the old creek bed, get our arms scratched up something awful by the brambles, but Lord it was worth it. You just can't find blackberries like that anymore. The ones in the store are all watery, got no taste to 'em. Same with the tomatoes, honestly. Look red enough, but you bite into 'em and they taste just like wet cardboard.
Over these past nine months, have you felt down, sad, or lost interest in your usual activities?

Down or sad? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I feel just fine, mostly. I mean, I still get out to the garden every morning. Well, when it's not raining, anyway. We've had an awful lot of rain lately, haven't we? Just buckets of it. The ground gets so muddy, you step out there and your boots sink right in, almost pulls 'em right off your feet. I remember back in '72, or maybe it was '73, we had rain like this for near on a month straight. Flooded the whole basement. Ruined my wife's good sewing machine, the Singer she got from her mother. She was heartbroken over that thing. We tried drying it out, putting it near the furnace, but it just rusted right up. They don't make them like they used to, you know. Everything's plastic now. You buy a toaster, it breaks in a year. The one we had when we first got married, all chrome and heavy as a brick, lasted us thirty years. Thirty years! Now you're lucky if you get it home from the store without it falling apart in the box.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits prominent persecutory ideas and delusions of reference (believing the domino players and radio announcer are transmitting coded warning messages specifically to him), alongside clear auditory hallucinations (hearing a friend call his name and hum choir songs when alone in the house). These psychotic symptoms have persisted intermittently for approximately nine months in the absence of significant affective disturbance, cognitive impairment, or underlying medical etiology, fulfilling the ICD-10 criteria for paranoid schizophrenia.

confirmed_symptoms: Ideas and delusions of reference (perceiving special, personal coded messages from men at the domino table and radio broadcasts)
Persecutory beliefs (interpreting the messages as warnings to be careful)
Auditory hallucinations (hearing an old friend's voice calling his name and humming choir songs when the house is empty)

additional_requirements: Absence of depressive or manic episodes concurrent with psychotic symptoms
